topics.topic: Authoritative JSON bytes and depth/size-check ownership for Python function outputs
questions: What exact JSON text exists for a returned Python value that has no canonical bytes, and which module creates and reports those bytes so `sandbox` can enforce `output_bytes` deterministically?

What is the "JSON text as returned" when agent code returns a Python object rather than JSON text, and which module creates and preserves those bytes so depth and output size can be checked before another walk or serialization fails?

What is the authoritative “JSON text as returned” for a Python object, which module creates and retains it, and which of `sandbox_runner`, `sandbox`, or `canonical_values` checks its depth and byte count before recursive serialization or validation can fail?

judgement.why: This is the same question about function-output JSON serialization, preservation, byte counting and depth enforcement already decided in P1 on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Boundary and interface for function-output fallback JSON serialization, byte counting, and depth checking
quotes: runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] When run returned, the program MUST write one returned message: whether the value is a dict with only str keys and, for each key, its form — json for a value port whose value json.dumps accepts with sort_keys=True, separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False and allow_nan=False (for a many value port, a list), file for a file port whose value is bytes, file_list for a many file port whose value is a list of bytes, not_representable otherwise and for a key that is no output port.

read_runner_report: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns RunnerReport with trap_hits, resource_hit, crashed, failure and returned (None when no complete returned line was read), each ReturnedOutput's json_text set only for form json and contents holding the file's bytes, or the list's in order, only for file and file_list.

judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation, the output ports and the bounds it is given and the release constants it imports, nothing else, and run nothing. The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output — for an output whose JSON text canonical_bytes refuses, the UTF-8 bytes of that text as returned — and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.
precedent.why: The later notes assign serialization to the runner, carry the resulting JSON text through RunnerReport, and assign canonicalization, fallback byte counting, and outcome judgment to sandbox.

topics.topic: Ownership and capability path for non-recursive raw-JSON depth measurement
questions: Which module owns the non-recursive raw-JSON depth scanner, and through which capability do `surface`, `installation`, `bindings`, `sandbox` and `service_invoker` use it before their parsers walk the text?

Which module owns the non-recursive depth-measurement mechanism used by `surface`, `canonical_values`, `sandbox`/`sandbox_runner`, `service_invoker`, `installation`, `bindings` and `run_values`, and through which allowed capability do the consumers use it?

Which module owns the non-recursive inspection of raw JSON text, and through what allowed dependency do `surface`, `installation`, `bindings`, `sandbox`/`sandbox_runner`, `service_invoker`, and `run_values` use it before parsing or otherwise walking the value?

judgement.why: This is the same question about ownership and dependency-safe use of the non-recursive JSON-depth mechanism already decided in P2 on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Ownership and dependency-safe exposure of the shared non-recursive JSON-depth validator
quotes: canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest element or member value, a member's name adding no level, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path is not an absolute path; it cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each component with os.O_NOFOLLOW, whose presence is never tested, each directory on the way also with os.O_PATH and os.O_DIRECTORY and the file itself also with os.O_NONBLOCK (A17), the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read, nest deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant — depth as canonical_bytes defines it, measured on the bytes without recursion before they are parsed —, or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name.

answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk.

read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON — a record nesting deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, depth as canonical_bytes defines it, measured without recursion before it is parsed, is not valid JSON —, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.
precedent.why: The later notes place canonical-value depth enforcement in canonical_values and explicitly make installation, surface, and bindings perform their own non-recursive ingress scans using the shared depth definition and release constant.

judgement.why: This is the same question about mapped-list depth enforcement, its run-facing failure result and its ownership already decided in P3 on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Release-pinned depth and size limits for grandfathered stored JSON and replayed mapped-list failures
quotes: The depth is measured on each JSON text where it enters the kernel, as a whole: the request message, each JSON text a request carries as a string (its own measure, the message adds nothing), each value output of a function, a service answer body that A09 parses, and a list assembled from mapped elements; a member's name adds no level.
A stored record entered that way and is never measured again; a later release that lowers the ceiling bounds only what enters after it (A20 rule 4).

assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it, or canonical_bytes refuses the list with NonCanonicalValueError — which for a list of stored canonical values happens only when it nests deeper than the release depth ceiling —, answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the json_text variant MUST return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of json_text, and for the bytes variant the hexadecimal SHA-256 of content exactly as given, without any canonicalization; this is the digest of a file and of a value's bytes.
precedent.why: The later texts distinguish stored canonical bytes, which are not remeasured or recanonicalized, from a mapped list assembled after an upgrade, which is a new entering value and therefore uses the current release ceilings.
